gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 9 build step already carries the direct `phase9-runtime-bitmap-sample-tests` leg and the focused `phase9-runtime-bitmap-top-bit-tests` leg, so the runtime starter and highest-valid-bit boundary replay stay visible beside the module, diff, loader, and survey gates without inventing a broader runtime substrate.
A bitmap-specific survey gate keeps the lib/test_bitmap.c anchor, starter status, focused highest-valid-bit replay, and remaining blockers explicit while the pilot surface stays small.
A sample-backed lifecycle starter is the first honest runtime-facing bitmap step that can reuse the existing bitmap-view helper without pretending the full module substrate already exists.
The Phase 9 roadmap explicitly calls for selftest hooks, and the bounded runtime_bitmap sample already keeps that requirement reviewable through descriptor metadata plus runSelftest().
A dedicated Phase 9 test file keeps the starter sample reviewable and bounded around lifecycle transitions, range mutation, copy, and summary behavior.
A narrow differential gate now captures a few lib/test_bitmap.c expectations for first-set, first-zero, weight, range mutation, and copy behavior before any broader runtime substrate work.

A tiny sample-side loader scaffold makes the existing requires_runtime_substrate contract reviewable through explicit entry and exit symbol names, handoff-stage checks, and a no-substrate release path without pretending a real module loader already exists.

The focused top-bit companion replay keeps the highest valid bit, one-bit boundary mutation, and immediate out-of-bounds guards reviewable through the shared Phase 9 bitmap packet without widening into full bitmap API parity.
A real loadable module entry point and lifecycle parity still depend on shared runtime substrate pieces that the repo has not started yet.
